speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
before: You want the key? You'll have to beat me for it! Yes, Chef! No - YOU, Chef!
after: So if it's the key you're after, you will have to win it from me in a duel, here and now, with the whole pantry watching! Yes, Chef! No - YOU, Chef!

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois
before: TASTE IT. TASTE IT! It's for the war effort!
after: TASTE IT! One little spoonful is all I ask, and you will never want anything else again. It's for the war effort!

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
before: Under-seasoned. NEXT!
after: Under-seasoned, the whole performance, from your first card to your last! NEXT!

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
before: The pantry door stays shut until you've learned to cook. Come back when you're properly seasoned!
after: The pantry door stays shut and the key stays on my apron. Go and simmer for a while, and come back whenever you like - I shall be right here, stirring!

speaker: Basil
before: Psst. I'm Basil, line cook - ladle in one hand, nerves in the other. We Gourmands feed the kingdom and protect it: the chefs cook and the golems guard. Lately, though, the golems have been... practising.
after: Psst. Over here. I'm Basil, a line cook, and I'm not supposed to be talking to anyone. We Gourmands feed the kingdom and guard it - the chefs cook, the golems guard - only lately the golems have been drilling.

speaker: Basil
before: Then she put the Special Sauce in every pot. The old rules still hold - nobody leaves hungry, nobody double-dips, and we say "Yes, Chef." Quietly. And nobody asks about the Test Kitchen. I'm not asking.
after: Then she put the Special Sauce in every pot. We still keep the old rules - nobody leaves hungry, nobody double-dips, and we say "Yes, Chef," only quietly now. And nobody asks about the Test Kitchen. I'm not asking.

speaker: Basil
before: You came back! Good, good. I've been stirring the same pot for an hour, just to give my hands something to do. A Gourmand never stops stirring.
after: Oh! You came back. Good, that's good. I've been stirring this same pot for an hour, because when my hands stop I start thinking, and I'd honestly rather stir.

speaker: Basil
before: What do we say? "Yes, Chef" - on the lowest possible heat.
after: Um, if anyone asks what the two of us talked about, we say "Yes, Chef," and we say it on the lowest possible heat, the way you'd keep a sauce from catching.

speaker: Basil
before: The Grand Chef has very good hearing, for someone who never tastes a thing.
after: The Grand Chef has very good hearing, you see. I've never understood how somebody can hear a whisper from the far side of the Pantry and never once want to taste a thing.

speaker: Basil
before: The real Chef baked a birthday cake for the little prince once. Four layers, one for each Path. He licked the frosting off all four and left the rest. ...Are you all right? You've gone pale.
after: Chef baked a birthday cake for the little prince once, back before all this - four layers, one for each Path - and he licked the frosting off all four and left the rest. ...Are you all right? You've gone pale.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: We're always out of something - honey, basil, ghost pepper. Half our deliveries go to the Test Kitchen and nothing comes back. I once fetched them a whole pig. Wrong pig, and he's still cross about it.
after: We're always out of something - honey, basil, ghost pepper - because half our deliveries go to the Test Kitchen and nothing ever comes back. I fetched them a whole pig once, the wrong pig, and he's still cross with me.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: Don't tell the Grand Chef I said anything. Last cook who complained got promoted to taste tester. We haven't seen him since.
after: Only please don't tell the Grand Chef I said any of that. The last cook who complained got promoted to taste tester, and we all clapped, and nobody's seen him since.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: Ingredients, please, anything? I'm one leaf away from calling this a salad and going home.
after: Have you got any ingredients on you, anything at all? I'm down to one lettuce leaf, and I'm seriously thinking of calling it a salad and going home.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: I'm so hungry I looked at a Refusemancer compost heap and thought 'starter'. Don't tell anyone. I'd never live it down.
after: I've been so busy feeding everyone else that I forgot to eat, and this morning I looked at a Refusemancer compost heap and thought 'starter'. Please don't tell anyone, I'd never live it down.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: Madame Mirepoix, darling: dessert dealer and card shark of the Grand Pantry. Tonight's tasting menu is three cards, lightly foiled, served with a little disdain.
after: Madame Mirepoix, my sweet: dessert dealer and card shark of the Grand Pantry. Tonight's tasting menu is three cards, lightly foiled, served with a little disdain.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: Every card is Gourmand-issue and, as of this year, inspected by the Test Kitchen. They stamped my decorative cake, darling, right on the rosette, and I have not forgiven them.
after: Every card is Gourmand-issue and, as of this year, inspected by the Test Kitchen. They stamped my decorative cake, my sweet, right on the rosette, and I have not forgiven them.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: I take gold, favours and sprinkles, in that order. I do not take the Special Sauce. I have been pretending to eat it for months.
after: I accept gold, favours and sprinkles, in that order, and I do not accept the Special Sauce. Between ourselves, I have been pretending to eat it for months, and I am a superb actress.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: Your cards are plated, darling; the cake is decorative. As for the Special Sauce, I recommend the air beside it.
after: Your cards are plated, my sweet, and the cake remains strictly decorative. As for the Special Sauce, since you were too polite to ask, I recommend the air beside it.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: You can fetch? Oh, wonderful. Our deliveries keep getting stolen and dropped all over the Buffet: there's truffle by the broccoli, salt by the river and honey up the Butte.
after: Wait, you can fetch? Oh, that's wonderful, because our deliveries keep getting stolen and then dropped all over the Buffet - there's truffle by the broccoli, salt by the river and honey up the Butte.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: Bring me any three and I'll make it worth your while. I'm begging with my whole apron here.
after: If you could bring me any three, I'd make it worth your while, I promise. I'd go myself, only I'm already late for four other things, and one of them was yesterday.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: Bring any three ingredients from around the Buffet. The pantry is empty, and I can't keep calling that a minimalist menu.
after: Any three ingredients from around the Buffet will do, I'm not fussy. The pantry's so empty that I've started telling people it's a minimalist menu, and I don't think they believe me.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: Three whole ingredients! The Pantry is saved - for today, anyway, which is the only day I'm worried about.
after: Three whole ingredients! Oh, you've saved the Pantry - well, you've saved it for today, and today is honestly the only day I've got room to worry about.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: Here, take this for your trouble. It's a card, and somehow it's also a soup. Soup you can play, if you can believe it.
after: Here, please take this for your trouble. It's a card, and somehow it's also a soup, and I've stopped asking how that works, because every time I ask, somebody hands me another list.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: The pantry's stocked until tomorrow, when we do it all again. I'm not complaining, I'm fetching. From a distance they look very similar.
after: The pantry's stocked until tomorrow, and then we do it all over again. I'm not complaining, mind, I'm fetching - although I'll admit that from a distance the two look very much alike.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: A favour, darling. A customer of mine wants a Hearty Pot Pie, a real one, and the Grand Oven is sulking. It keeps being asked to cook prototypes.
after: A favour, my sweet. A customer of mine has asked for a Hearty Pot Pie, a real one, and the Grand Oven is sulking, because it has been made to cook nothing but prototypes all year.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: Bake one for me: honey, giant basil and a ghost pepper, into the Grand Oven by the arch, then bring it here. Careful with the pepper. It is not a team player.
after: Bake one for me: honey, giant basil and a ghost pepper, into the Grand Oven by the arch, and then bring the pie here to me. Do be careful with the pepper, which has never collaborated with anyone.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: One Hearty Pot Pie, darling. Honey, basil and a ghost pepper into the Grand Oven by the arch. I shall wait. I have a cake to look at.
after: One Hearty Pot Pie, my sweet: honey, basil and a ghost pepper, into the Grand Oven by the arch, and then back here to me. I shall wait, and I have a cake to admire in the meantime.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: A pie. A real one, golden and warm. My customer is going to cry.
after: A pie. A real one, golden and warm, and it smells the way this Pantry used to smell before the sauce. My customer is going to cry.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: And so am I, discreetly. Here is your reward, you scrappy little thing, and thank you.
after: And so shall I, discreetly, once you have gone. Here is your reward, my sweet, and thank you - I do not say that to everyone, so kindly do not spread it about.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: The best pie this Pantry has seen in years. The oven would like a word with you. I believe it wants to say thank you.
after: That was the best pie this Pantry has seen in years, my sweet. The Grand Oven would like a word with you, and I believe the word is thank you.

speaker: Basil
before: Um, could I have a word? Quietly? Old Meatloaf, our oldest golem, has stopped working. The Test Kitchen tried to strip him for parts, and we only got him back in two pieces. He hasn't spoken since Tuesday.
after: Um, could I have a word? Quietly? It's Old Meatloaf, our oldest golem. The Test Kitchen tried to strip him for parts, and we only got him back in two pieces, and he hasn't said a word since Tuesday.

speaker: Basil
before: He needs sea salt for his joints, from the Salt Flats by the river, and a black truffle for his heart, from under the Broccoli Forest to the south-west. Mend him and Sir Loin will let you through the Layer-Cake Town gate. Yes, Chef? ...Please?
after: He needs sea salt for his joints, from the Salt Flats by the river, and a black truffle for his heart, from under the Broccoli Forest to the south-west. Mend him and Sir Loin opens the Layer-Cake Town gate. Yes, Chef?

speaker: Basil
before: Sea salt is out on the Salt Flats, by the river. The black truffle grows under the Broccoli Forest's trees, south-west of here. Both are marked on your map.
after: The sea salt is out on the Salt Flats, by the river, and the black truffle grows under the Broccoli Forest's trees, south-west of here. They're both marked on your map - I checked twice.

speaker: Basil
before: Old Meatloaf is over by the west wall of the Grand Pantry. Sea salt, a black truffle, and a bit of tenderness.
after: Old Meatloaf is over by the west wall of the Grand Pantry. He needs the sea salt and the black truffle and, um, a bit of tenderness, if you've got any to spare.

speaker: Basil
before: He's walking, and he's sizzling! Old Meatloaf is back on duty! I'm not crying, I'm just standing near some onions.
after: He's walking! Old Meatloaf is walking and sizzling, and he's back at his post as if nothing ever happened! I'm not crying, I just happen to be standing very near some onions.

speaker: Basil
before: Here's your reward, and Sir Loin will open his gate for you now. Well done. Yes, Chef.
after: Here, this is your reward, and Sir Loin will open his gate for you now. Well done. I mean it, I couldn't have gone out there myself. ...Yes, Chef.

speaker: Basil
before: Old Meatloaf is the best golem in the kingdom. Don't tell the others. They know.
after: Old Meatloaf is the best golem in the whole kingdom, and I'd ask you not to tell the others, except I think they've always known.

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: He says it to you, though you are not a chef. He doesn't mind.
after: He says it to you, although you are not a chef, and he does not seem to mind in the least.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Appointments. Let's see now... you're not down for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.
after: Oh, only appointments. Let's see now... no, you're not down for a good long while yet, and that's just what I like to see. Lovely! Heh.

speaker: Colonel Casserole
before: Halt, traveller! This gate opens only for a duel of honour, so lids up. Yes, Chef.
after: Halt there, traveller! This gate opens for nothing but a duel of honour, fairly fought, so lids up, and may the better dish win. Yes, Chef.

speaker: Colonel Casserole
before: En garde! Thirty years of service, and I have never once boiled over. Until now. Yes, Chef.
after: En garde! In thirty years of service I have never once boiled over, and I had hoped to retire with that record intact, but you do press a casserole hard. Yes, Chef.

speaker: (narration)
before: You pour a vat out. Behind it, a service door opens on the Executive Test Kitchen. The air there smells like a very expensive soup that nobody has ever tasted.
after: You pour a vat out, and behind it a service door opens on the Executive Test Kitchen, where the air smells like a very expensive soup that nobody has ever tasted.

speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
before: And what is THIS? A civilian, unsupervised, in my bay, with flavour on his breath. Disgraceful.
after: And what is THIS? A civilian, wandering about my bay unsupervised, with flavour on his breath! You are out of uniform and out of bounds, soldier, and I call it a disgrace.

speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
before: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense, and you will stand up straight when you hear it. Taste is a weakness, son. Paste is a strategy.
after: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense, and you will stand up straight when you hear it. Taste is a weakness, soldier. Paste is a strategy.

speaker: The Doppelganger
before: They always asked whether I tasted the soup. ...I never did. I never could.
after: They were always asking whether I had tasted the soup. ...I never did, and I do not think that I ever could.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You never taste your own soup, do you?
after: Every cook I met on the way here told me the same thing, and all of them whispered it. You never taste your own soup, do you?

speaker: (narration)
before: Beneath it, you see a shifting shadow in a spotless white coat.
after: Beneath it there is only a shifting shadow in a spotless white coat.

speaker: (narration)
before: Behind the shadow, you see the unfinished war machines standing still.
after: Behind the shadow, the unfinished war machines stand in their rows and do not move.

speaker: Basil
before: It wasn't her. It was a Doppelganger, wearing her face for ten years, and you walked right up to it. I'd have fainted. I did faint, earlier, about something else.
after: It wasn't her! All that time it was a Doppelganger wearing her face, for ten whole years, and you just walked right up to it. I'd have fainted. I did faint, um, earlier, about something else.

speaker: Basil
before: She remembered the cake. The very first thing she said when we opened the freezer was "Is the boy all right?" I didn't know what to tell her.
after: And she remembered the cake, all four layers of it. The very first thing she said when we got the freezer open was "Is the boy all right?" and I didn't know what to tell her. I still don't.

speaker: Basil
before: The Special Sauce is down the drain and the golems guard plates again. Yes, Chef. I can say it out loud now. I keep saying it to the walls, just to hear it.
after: The Special Sauce has all gone down the drain, and the golems are back to guarding plates. Yes, Chef! I can say it out loud now, and I keep saying it to the walls just to hear how it sounds.

speaker: Basil
before: Take seconds. You've earned seconds. You've earned thirds. Listen to me, I'm not even whispering.
after: Please, take seconds. You've earned seconds, and thirds if you can manage them, and... oh, listen to me, I'm not even whispering any more.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: Tarragon, Sous-Chef and fetcher of things! Sorry, I'm out of breath. I finally caught up with lunch.
after: Tarragon, Sous-Chef and fetcher of things! Sorry, give me a second, I'm out of breath - I finally caught up with lunch, and it turns out I'd run straight past it twice.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: Ingredients are coming back from the Test Kitchen by the cartload, pigs included, and this time the pig is happy about it. I've had quite enough professional disagreements with pigs.
after: Ingredients are coming back from the Test Kitchen by the cartload, pigs included, and this time the pig's happy about it, which is a relief, because I've had quite enough professional disagreements with pigs.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: People wave when I fetch things now, and nobody's asked me for a single cannonball. Flour, eggs, a little thyme... sorry, I'm making lists again.
after: People wave at me when I fetch things now, and nobody's asked me for a single cannonball all week. It's just flour, eggs, a little thyme... sorry, I'm making lists again, only this time I'm enjoying it.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: Madame Mirepoix, free of the sauce. My taste buds came back last week, and darling... the sugar. I wept into a meringue.
after: Madame Mirepoix, free of the sauce at last. My taste buds came back last week, my sweet, and the sugar... I wept into a meringue, and I must say the meringue was improved by it.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: Cakes by day, cards by night. All by appointment, and all by choice.
after: I do cakes by day and cards by night, all of it by appointment and, for the first time in ten years, all of it by choice.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: Sit down and have a slice, darling. The cake has been promoted from decoration to dessert.
after: Sit down and have a slice, my sweet. The cake has been promoted from decoration to dessert, and it has taken the news very graciously.

speaker: Basil
before: The Colonel's gone. He cleared out his office overnight and took the paste recipe with him.
after: Um. The Colonel's gone. He cleared out his whole office overnight, and he took the paste recipe with him, though I can't think why he'd need to.

speaker: Basil
before: It's one word long, and the word is 'paste'.
after: I've seen that recipe, you see, and it's only one word long, and the word is 'paste'.

speaker: The Grand Chef (formerly Grand Chef Escoffina)
before: Grey food, from a tap. Somebody ought to teach that man to cook.
after: Grey food out of a tap, for a whole city. Somebody ought to sit that man down at a table and teach him what cooking is for.
